newsitem.title: DUBAI: Iran, Syria leaders discuss Mideast, cooperation.
newsitem.headline: Iran, Syria leaders discuss Mideast, cooperation.

text.p: Iranian President Akbar Hashemi Rafsanjani called for a continued struggle against the "Zionist regime" in talks with Syrian President Hafez al-Assad in Tehran, Iran's official news agency IRNA said.
In their first round of talks after Assad's arrival in Tehran, the two leaders also discussed regional developments and the need to boost ties among Islamic states, IRNA said late on Thursday.
"The Iranian president said that the Islamic Republic...stressed the need for struggling against the Zionist regime," the agency said.

Iran and Israel have been bitter enemies since Iran's 1979 Islamic revolution. Iran says Israel has no right to exist and has been vehemently opposed to the Middle East peace process since its inception.

"The presidents of Iran and Syria...stressed the need for safeguarding Iraq's territorial integrity, for broadening regional cooperation between Iran and Syria, for the ouster of foreign troops in the Persian Gulf, for supporting the righteous cause and struggle of the people of Palestine, and for closer collaboration between Moslem nations," IRNA said.
Iran opposes the presence of Western forces in the Gulf, saying security is the responsibility of regional states.

There are some 20,000 U.S. troops deployed in and around the Gulf. Part of the forces are used to enforce United Nations sanctions against Iraq. The United States has vowed to protect its Gulf Arab allies from any potential Iranian security threat.
Iran says the presence of U.S. forces in the Gulf is the biggest threat to regional security.
Assad arrived in Tehran on Thursday on his second visit to the Islamic republic since the 1979 revolution.
